clue.text: Come to an end-yet proceed!

definitions.meaning: to expire or lapse, as a deadline or a mood does
to go on or move past, as traffic does at a junction

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone onward even as things wind down.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both lapsing, as a moment that goes by, and moving onward, as when told to go along.

clue.text: Being on the wrong side of the law, they're our enemies

definitions.text: Being on the wrong side of the law, they're our enemies

parts.words: Being on the wrong side of the law, they're our enemies
parts.note: from a criminal's view, those who enforce the law are the foes

explanation.definitionFit: Officers of the force are the natural enemies of anyone who breaks the law.

clue.text: Here, aim for the fun of the fair!

definitions.text: Here, aim for the fun of the fair!

parts.words: Here, aim for the fun of the fair!
parts.note: a funfair stall where players aim rifles at targets for prizes

explanation.definitionFit: Fairground stalls with rifles and moving targets are where people aim for fun.

clue.text: Mean to get drunk

explanation.surface: A miser sets out to get inebriated.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word both for a miser's closed fist and for someone who has had too much to drink.

clue.text: Men rotted, horribly hurt like this

indicators.note: the letters of Men rotted are horribly jumbled

explanation.surface: Men left rotting have been cruelly hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tortured or made to suffer greatly is to be hurt badly.

clue.text: Greedily eat a big hole in the ground!

definitions.text: a big hole in the ground
definitions.meaning: a deep narrow valley or ravine

explanation.surface: A glutton gobbles at a huge ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to stuff oneself with food and a steep-sided ravine.

clue.text: They may record these bands

definitions.meaning: cassettes or reels used for recording sound

explanation.surface: Groups of musicians may be recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' suggests musicians, but means narrow strips.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both recording cassettes and narrow strips of fabric.

clue.text: Pick up sound information from some Israelis coming back

definitions.note: the clue describes what the organs do; the answer is the organs themselves

indicators.note: the run taken from Israelis is read from right to left, returning
only some letters of the word Israelis are used, a run lying within it

explanation.surface: Someone gathers news from Israelis returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes SRAE from inside Israelis and 'coming back' turns it round. The definition describes the organs by their job rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: These organs of hearing are what detect and collect sound for the brain.

clue.text: Finishes a written statement of forceful kind

definitions.text: Finishes a written statement of forceful kind

parts.words: Finishes a written statement of forceful kind
parts.note: the punctuation sign placed at the end of an emphatic sentence

explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark closes an emphatic or exclaimed sentence in writing.

clue.text: We go at this in a big hurry!

definitions.text: We go at this in a big hurry!

parts.words: We go at this in a big hurry!
parts.note: going at a great rate when rushing

explanation.definitionFit: Rapid motion or velocity is what one moves with when rushing.

clue.text: Worker left this party with hesitation

parts.note: the Labour Party is Britain's main left-wing party
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A worker quits a party, having dithered first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb meaning quit; it is part of the description of a left-wing party, the UK Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual worker is commonly called a hand or toiler, and this word names such a person.

clue.text: How to conserve food: take it from the tree before the French

indicators.note: the picking piece comes ahead of the French article

parts.note: to pick fruit is to take it from the tree

explanation.surface: Advice on preserving fruit: harvest it before a French cook does.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserving vegetables in vinegar or brine is a traditional way to keep them from spoiling.

clue.text: Nothing could be further from extremes than this!

definitions.text: Nothing could be further from extremes than this!

parts.words: Nothing could be further from extremes than this!
parts.note: a boast of moderation that literally describes the point equidistant from all edges

explanation.definitionFit: The middle point is by definition as far as possible from every edge or extreme.

clue.text: Got from the ranks of the free

definitions.text: Got from the ranks of the free

parts.words: Got from the ranks of the free
parts.note: reads like recruiting from free people, but means removed from freedom, made into a captive worker

explanation.definitionFit: To be taken from the free and placed in bondage is to be made a slave.

clue.text: Attracts wild gnat; me, too

definitions.note: a verb, while the answer is the noun naming a thing that attracts

indicators.note: the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A gnat swarms after someone, and they are drawn to it as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges GNAT and ME. The definition is a verb describing what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of iron with this property pulls metal objects towards it.

clue.text: From Cairo, a Mediterranean tripper certainly got about

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the words Cairo, a Mediterranean, running across them

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker based in Cairo really travelled around the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'Cairo, a Mediterranean'; 'tripper certainly' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel widely without a fixed route is to wander.

clue.text: Holds back and takes break in bad weather

parts.note: to rest is to take a break
rains are spells of wet weather

explanation.surface: Someone stays put and takes a break while it pours.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or check something is to keep it from moving forward.

clue.text: Takes on special cover for an important occasion

definitions.text: Takes on special cover for an important occasion

parts.words: Takes on special cover for an important occasion
parts.note: putting on smart clothes for a grand event

explanation.definitionFit: Putting on formal or fancy clothes is the usual way to prepare for a big event.

clue.text: Worried in a wordy way!

parts.note: worried here means pestered, done with words: repeated complaining

explanation.definitionFit: Persistent verbal fault-finding is the classic way to pester someone.

clue.text: To take one's breath away is felt to be wrong

indicators.note: the letters of is felt are set wrongly, in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Being left breathless is thought to be a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother or suffocate is literally to cut off someone's breathing.

clue.text: Assembles for prayers

definitions.meaning: short set prayers in the Christian liturgy

explanation.surface: Someone gathers people together for worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a noun stressed on the first syllable: short prayers said on set days in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gathers together and, as a noun, brief liturgical prayers.

clue.text: Ancient god bowed — but certainly not with age!

definitions.text: Ancient god bowed — but certainly not with age!

parts.words: Ancient god bowed — but certainly not with age!
parts.note: bowed suggests stooped with age, but the Roman love god carries a bow and is pictured as a child

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is shown as a boy with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Boat coming from the ocean

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the letters of ocean, rearranged

explanation.surface: A small vessel arriving from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A light narrow vessel paddled by hand is a small boat.

clue.text: In a sense, flighty piece often helps us up!

definitions.text: In a sense, flighty piece often helps us up!

parts.words: In a sense, flighty piece often helps us up!
parts.note: flighty suggests a fickle person, but means part of a flight of steps

explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a flight is what lifts us from one floor to the next.

clue.text: High-rearing mounts often found in them

definitions.text: High-rearing mounts often found in them

parts.words: High-rearing mounts often found in them
parts.note: mounts suggests horses rearing up, but means mountains, which stand in long chains

explanation.definitionFit: Mountain chains are where tall peaks are grouped together.

clue.text: Traditionally, fat beast mauls one bird

parts.note: the pig is traditionally pictured as fat

indicators.note: one is mauled, its letters knocked about

explanation.surface: A fat animal attacks a single bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock dove and its city descendants are a familiar kind of bird.

clue.text: Steam, in a coil, gets things brisk and lively

indicators.note: the letters are wound into a coil and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Steam coiling round gets machinery moving briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to life or enliven is to make something move with vigour.

clue.text: Sort of tax job that we ought to do!

definitions.meaning: a levy on goods, as customs or excise

definitions.text: job that we ought to do
definitions.meaning: an obligation, something one is bound to perform

explanation.surface: Paying a particular tax is an obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a levy on imports and a moral obligation.

clue.text: Laser cut out some of the upper crust

indicators.note: the word Laser is cut up and its letters laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A laser trims away part of a pie's top crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers of this rank belong to the aristocracy, the upper crust of society.

clue.text: Last backward look-that's sly

indicators.note: the sly look is written backward

parts.note: a peek is a sly, quick look

explanation.surface: A final glance behind, done craftily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' is a verb here, meaning endure or remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or remain in good condition is to hold up over time.
